title: Advanced comparison
note: modifying the comparative and the equative (much/far/a great deal/considerably/somewhat up, slightly/a little/marginally down, no + comparative, nowhere near / nothing like / every bit before as…as) and why very and too cannot · correlative the … the plus the doubled comparative and increasingly · the as … as frame: multiplied, negated, quantifier agreement, as good a N as, the same as vs similar to · choosing the frame: fewer vs less, the comparative for two of a kind, than vs then, than + clause, prefer X to Y vs would rather X than Y, by far + superlative · deliberately avoids ground owned elsewhere: plain -er/-est formation (a2_comparatives), no sooner and the other inverted negative adverbials (c1_inversion_emphasis), verb-phrase ellipsis in the than-clause (c1_ellipsis_substitution) · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 17)

cards.title: The comparative has its own modifiers
cards.body: A comparative cannot be modified by very, quite or too — those belong to the plain adjective. The comparative takes its own set of scalers: much, far, a lot, a great deal, considerably and somewhat push it up; slightly, a little, a bit and marginally hold it down; and no comparative at all is the flat denial in there is no better time. The equative scales too, with nowhere near, nothing like and every bit standing in front of as … as. The English is far more expensive, never very more expensive. Czech reaches for mnohem, podstatně, o něco and zdaleka ne, and the mapping is close enough to trust: where Czech says mnohem, English says much or far, and where Czech says o něco, English says slightly or a little.
cards.body_cz: Komparativ nelze stupňovat pomocí very, quite ani too — ta patří k základnímu tvaru přídavného jména. Komparativ má vlastní sadu zesilovačů: much, far, a lot, a great deal, considerably a somewhat jej posouvají nahoru, slightly, a little, a bit a marginally jej drží při zemi a samotné no je rovnou popření, jako v there is no better time. Stupňovat lze i vazbu as … as, a to pomocí nowhere near, nothing like a every bit. Správně je far more expensive, nikdy very more expensive. Čeština volí mnohem, podstatně, o něco a zdaleka ne, a převod je natolik pravidelný, že se na něj dá spolehnout: kde čeština řekne mnohem, angličtina řekne much nebo far, a kde čeština řekne o něco, angličtina řekne slightly nebo a little.
points: very, quite and too modify the plain adjective, never the comparative.
much cheaper is right; very cheaper is not English.
The same scalers work in front of as … as.

cards.title: the … the
cards.body: Two comparatives can be locked together so that one rises with the other, and English does it with the … the: the more you listen, the easier it becomes. Both halves need the article, both comparatives come to the front of their own clause, and the second half may drop its verb altogether — the sooner we leave, the better. This is the direct counterpart of Czech čím … tím, and the trap is leaving out the first the, which Czech gives no reason to expect. The same idea over time is carried by a doubled comparative — more and more expensive, better and better, fewer and fewer people — or by increasingly before the plain adjective. Note that people are counted, so the doubling is fewer and fewer, not less and less.
cards.body_cz: Dva komparativy lze spojit tak, že jeden roste s druhým; angličtina k tomu užívá vazbu the … the: the more you listen, the easier it becomes. Obě části potřebují člen, oba komparativy stojí na začátku své věty a v druhé části může sloveso zcela vypadnout — the sooner we leave, the better. Jde o přímý protějšek českého čím … tím a nástraha spočívá ve vypuštění prvního the, k němuž čeština nedává žádný důvod. Tentýž vývoj v čase vyjadřuje zdvojený komparativ — more and more expensive, better and better, fewer and fewer people — nebo increasingly před základním tvarem. Lidé se počítají, a proto je správně fewer and fewer, nikoli less and less.
points: Czech čím … tím maps onto it directly, but English needs both articles.
The second clause may drop its verb: the sooner, the better.
Over time, double the comparative instead: more and more expensive.

cards.title: as … as
cards.body: As … as states equality, and everything interesting happens around it. It scales by multiplication — twice as expensive, three times as much, half as much — where Czech prefers dvakrát dražší and the as … as frame has to be built rather than translated. Negated, it becomes not as … as or the slightly more formal not so … as. With a countable noun inside it the quantifier must agree: as many people, as much time. Two patterns are worth learning whole: the article moves inside in as good a teacher as I have ever met, and equality with a noun is the same as, never the same like or the same than, while similar takes to. Nothing like and every bit scale the equative the way far and slightly scale the comparative.
cards.body_cz: Vazba as … as vyjadřuje rovnost a všechno zajímavé se odehrává kolem ní. Násobí se — twice as expensive, three times as much, half as much — zatímco čeština volí dvakrát dražší, takže vazbu as … as je nutné postavit, nikoli přeložit. V záporu zní not as … as nebo o něco formálněji not so … as. Stojí-li uvnitř počitatelné podstatné jméno, musí souhlasit i kvantifikátor: as many people, as much time. Dvě vazby stojí za to si zapamatovat celé: člen se přesouvá dovnitř ve spojení as good a teacher as I have ever met, a rovnost s podstatným jménem se vyjadřuje pomocí the same as, nikdy the same like ani the same than, kdežto similar se pojí s to. Nothing like a every bit stupňují vazbu as … as stejně jako far a slightly stupňují komparativ.

cards.title: Choosing the frame
cards.body: At C1 the work is choosing the right frame, not forming the comparative. Fewer counts, less measures — fewer than twenty people, less time. With exactly two things English uses the comparative with the article, the more experienced of the two, and saves the superlative for three or more. Than is the comparative conjunction and then is a time word; they are not interchangeable, and than is followed by a full clause whenever the comparison needs one — faster than I do. Preference splits by pattern: prefer X to Y, but would rather X than Y. By far reinforces a superlative where much would reinforce a comparative, and a comparison can be closed off from the other side entirely — no other candidate was as popular.
cards.body_cz: Na úrovni C1 nejde o tvoření komparativu, ale o volbu správné vazby. Fewer se pojí s počitatelnými, less s nepočitatelnými — fewer than twenty people, less time. Jsou-li porovnávány právě dvě věci, užívá angličtina komparativ se členem, the more experienced of the two, a superlativ si nechává pro tři a více. Than je spojka srovnání, then je časové příslovce a zaměnit je nelze; po than následuje celá věta všude tam, kde to srovnání vyžaduje — faster than I do. Vyjádření preference se dělí podle vazby: prefer X to Y, ale would rather X than Y. By far zesiluje superlativ tam, kde by much zesiloval komparativ, a srovnání lze uzavřít i z druhé strany — no other candidate was as popular.

the most experienced of the two

points: Two of a kind take the comparative with the: the more experienced of the two.
by far goes with a superlative; much goes with a comparative.

items.gap: ____ than twenty people applied.

items.explanation: At C1 the work is choosing the right frame, not forming the comparative. Fewer counts, less measures — fewer than twenty people, less time. With exactly two things English uses the comparative with the article, the more experienced of the two, and saves the superlative for three or more. Than is the comparative conjunction and then is a time word; they are not interchangeable, and than is followed by a full clause whenever the comparison needs one — faster than I do. Preference splits by pattern: prefer X to Y, but would rather X than Y. By far reinforces a superlative where much would reinforce a comparative, and a comparison can be closed off from the other side entirely — no other candidate was as popular.
items.explanation_cz: Na úrovni C1 nejde o tvoření komparativu, ale o volbu správné vazby. Fewer se pojí s počitatelnými, less s nepočitatelnými — fewer than twenty people, less time. Jsou-li porovnávány právě dvě věci, užívá angličtina komparativ se členem, the more experienced of the two, a superlativ si nechává pro tři a více. Than je spojka srovnání, then je časové příslovce a zaměnit je nelze; po than následuje celá věta všude tam, kde to srovnání vyžaduje — faster than I do. Vyjádření preference se dělí podle vazby: prefer X to Y, ale would rather X than Y. By far zesiluje superlativ tam, kde by much zesiloval komparativ, a srovnání lze uzavřít i z druhé strany — no other candidate was as popular.
